figures.source: Most UK vs Australia comparisons treat the 1-year vs 2-year gap as a footnote and jump straight to rankings or "which country is friendlier." That skips the part that actually shapes your money, your visa timeline, and your job search: a UK masters compresses everything (coursework, dissertation, networking, and job hunting) into 12 months, while an Australian masters spreads the same weight across 24 months with more room for internships and slower-building networks.

items.text: The UK's cost advantage is not really about UK universities being "cheap", several UK programs charge more per year than equivalent Australian ones.
This is the factor that should carry the most weight, and the one general "UK vs Australia" articles skip the most.

London's financial sector gives the UK unmatched depth for banking, asset management, and fintech roles that Australia's smaller financial centres (Sydney, Melbourne) cannot fully match at graduate level.

The UK's legal and policy ecosystem, built around centuries of institutional depth, gives graduate-level entry points that Australia's smaller, more localised legal market does not offer at the same scale.

blocks.heading: Program Length 1 Year
rows: Program length
1 year (most taught masters)
2 years (most coursework masters)
Tuition
Roughly £10,000-38,000 for the full 1-year program (Rs 10.7L-40.7L at current rates)
Roughly AUD 20,000-45,000 per year (Rs 14L-33L per year), charged across 2 years
Living costs
Roughly Rs 10-14 lakh for the single year (accommodation, food, transport, insurance)
Roughly AUD 1,500-2,500/month (Rs 97,700-1.63 lakh/month), charged across 2 years, plus upfront Overseas Student Health Cover
Rough total, full program
Roughly Rs 39-58 lakh
Roughly Rs 57-93 lakh
Where the money actually goes
Tuition and one year of city living costs, mostly in a single compressed cycle
The second year is the real cost driver: an extra year of tuition, an extra year of rent, and health cover you would not pay in the UK's shorter timeline

blocks.heading: Sponsored Settlement Vs Points-Tested PR
rows: Post-study work window
2 years (18 months from 1 January 2027 for masters graduates)
Up to 3 years for masters graduates (with AI-ECTA extra year for Indian passport holders)
Route to settlement
Must switch to an employer-sponsored Skilled Worker visa, then usually build 5 years of continuous sponsored residence before applying for Indefinite Leave to Remain
Points-tested system (subclass 189, 190, or 491); no employer sponsorship required for 189, though a competitive score usually needs more than the 65-point floor
What decides your odds
Finding one employer willing to sponsor you under the Skilled Worker route, at the required salary level for your role

Accumulated points across age, English score, education, skilled work experience, and occupation-list eligibility; recent invitations for the main points-tested stream typically need 80-90+ points, well above the 65-point minimum
Occupation dependency
Sponsorship is available across most graduate-level roles, not limited to a fixed skilled-occupation list
Points-tested PR is tied to specific skilled-occupation lists; being outside a listed occupation makes the points route far harder regardless of your points score

blocks.heading: UK Is Cheaper As a Full

figures.label: Total Education Cost
figures.source: The UK is cheaper as a full package for most students. A 1-year UK masters plus 12 months of living costs typically lands in the roughly Rs 39-58 lakh range. A 2-year Australian masters costs less per year in some tuition brackets, but the second year of tuition, an extra year of living costs, upfront Overseas Student Health Cover, and a steep visa application fee push the Australian total to roughly Rs 57-93 lakh. The gap is mostly the extra year, not a difference in how "expensive" each country is per year.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: Australia gives a longer initial runway and a real points-based path to permanent residence: master's graduates get up to 3 years on the Subclass 485 visa (including the extra year Indian passport holders get under the Australia-India trade agreement), and skilled-occupation-list roles can lead to a 189, 190, or 491 points-tested PR visa. The UK's Graduate Route gives 2 years of unrestricted work rights for people who apply by 31 December 2026 (18 months for masters graduates who apply from 1 January 2027), but it is explicitly not a settlement route, you have to switch into the employer-sponsored Skilled Worker visa and build years of sponsored work before you can apply for permanent settlement (Indefinite Leave to Remain). If long-term settlement is your main goal and you are not chasing one specific UK employer, Australia's pathway is the more direct one on paper.

items.text: A 1-year masters means you are job-hunting almost from the day you arrive; there is very little slack for a slow start.
The UK's Indian community is older and deeply established, especially in London, Leicester, and Birmingham, with generations of infrastructure already in place.
The compressed academic calendar means dissertation deadlines and job applications often overlap directly, which is a real stress point most UK program pages do not mention upfront.
